summary: Feed s134_double is degraded for APM: 74.3% of TCP sessions are one-way and 3.0% of packets show drops. APM requires bidirectional traffic and will have incomplete transaction/latency visibility.

findings.root_cause: 74.3% of TCP sessions (81/109) show only one direction, well above 10% threshold. Most likely only one direction is being tapped/SPANned or packet broker is not aggregating both RX and TX to the same tool port, or asymmetric routing with incomplete capture.
findings.impact_on_tool: APM needs_both_directions=true to correlate request/response for latency and transaction timing. With single-direction traffic it cannot measure response time, status codes, or complete transactions, causing blind spots and false performance metrics.

recommended_fix.why: Aggregate both sides of each flow to the same APM port so the tool sees complete client-server conversations for accurate APM analysis.

findings.root_cause: 3.0% of TCP packets (30/1012) show sequence gaps/missing data, above 1% threshold. Tool overload is healthy, so drops are in the visibility path - typically SPAN port oversubscription/buffer exhaustion or packet broker ingress drops, not tool ingress overload.
findings.impact_on_tool: Even though APM needs_full_payload=false, missing packets break TCP reassembly, causing inaccurate latency/retransmission counts, incomplete transaction records and gaps in application performance monitoring.

recommended_fix.why: TAP provides lossless line-rate copy versus SPAN which drops under load. Replacing SPAN with TAP (and checking broker oversubscription) eliminates the 3% loss and restores complete packet delivery.
